records.c:
Purpose: Central Park phase handoff installed by the first expanded segment and retained after the second. Inputs: completed level load and restored low workspace. Outputs: unconditional transfer to `$8EAD`; does not return. Assumptions: Central Park playable occupant `$4E00-$FEFF` is active. Clobbers: none before transfer. Hardware changes: none in this veneer.
function: undefined PhaseHandoff()

Purpose: tail-call the resident C64/level initializer at `$0E00` through Central Park's retained phase vector. Inputs: none. Outputs: cleared runtime work areas, installed interrupt state, and initialized VIC-II, CIA, SID, banking, and NMI-vector state. Assumptions: the Central Park retained vector and resident initializer are intact and real C64 I/O is present. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, zero-page/game state, and screen workspaces. Hardware changes: the target selects `$01=$35`, disables CIA interrupts, clears VIC-II interrupt/sprite state, silences SID, installs NMI vectors, and synchronizes to the raster; the veneer adds no stack frame.

Runtime title-render marker read at $1EEE; nonzero is cleared and triggers music reinitialization through $4000. Boot/title setup also clears it at $110D. The marker is one byte; six trailing captured zero bytes have no established independent role.

Purpose: initialize Central Park's retained SID music module. Inputs: A selects the song. Outputs: initialized music state. Assumptions: retained module and gameplay phase match. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and music state. Hardware changes: initializes state later emitted to SID.

Purpose: service one Central Park music tick. Inputs: initialized sequencer state. Outputs: advanced tracks and SID register image. Assumptions: the retained module matches the active gameplay phase. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and music state. Hardware changes: writes SID registers.

Purpose: set Central Park's three music-control bytes from A. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: updated player controls. Assumptions: module active. Clobbers: flags and music scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: increment Central Park's music gate/pause state. Inputs: module active. Outputs: incremented gate byte. Assumptions: retained player state is valid. Clobbers: flags. Hardware changes: none directly.

42 ASCII bytes through $4035: MUSIC BY R. OUWEHAND AND PLAYER BY F. PAUL. Retained credit string between the music entry veneers and runtime state; no display consumer is established in the loaded Central Park phase. These are authored text, not an unidentified sound table.

records.c: Purpose: implement Central Park's retained music sequencer and track-bytecode parser. Inputs: song descriptor, three voice streams, and player state. Outputs: updated music/SID state. Assumptions: retained code and sequence tables are from the same level title. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and player state. Hardware changes: writes SID registers during tick service.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4006 music-control veneer by storing A into the module's three control bytes and returning.
Inputs: A is the control value; the matching retained music occupant and its writable state are active.
Outputs: A is stored to $403D-$403F; A, X, Y, and all status flags are preserved on return.
Assumptions: The three adjacent bytes are the control triplet for this exact music-module occupant.
Clobbers: Memory $403D-$403F; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written directly.

Purpose: copy A into the paired global music-control bytes. Inputs: A is the control value. Outputs: both control bytes equal A; A, X, Y, and flags are preserved. Assumptions: Central Park music-player occupant is active. Clobbers: memory only. Hardware changes: none directly; the later music service consumes the state.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4003 music-tick veneer, honoring the module gate and advancing its sequencer and SID image.
Inputs: The module is initialized; $4038 is its gate byte and the resident IRQ enters through the matching $4003 veneer.
Outputs: Advances or gates the current music tick, updates sequencer/envelope state, emits the resulting SID register values, and returns.
Assumptions: The retained title/play music module matches the active phase and the call occurs at the engine's normal music-tick cadence.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, zero-page music cursors, module track/envelope state, and SID register state.
Hardware changes: Writes SID voice and filter/volume registers as directed by the current tick; no CIA or VIC-II access is introduced by the veneer body.

Purpose: Implement Level's $4009 gate veneer by incrementing the module gate byte and returning.
Inputs: $4038 is the writable gate byte for the matching retained music occupant.
Outputs: $4038 is incremented modulo 256; N and Z describe the new value; A, X, and Y are preserved.
Assumptions: The caller intentionally changes the module gate/pause state and accepts byte wraparound.
Clobbers: $4038, N, and Z; A, X, Y, C, V, D, and I are preserved, and RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Hardware changes: No hardware registers are written directly.

Purpose: fetch and interpret the next note or effect command for a voice. Inputs: phase-local voice index, stream pointers, and player state. Outputs: stream cursors, note/effect parameters, and target-frequency state are updated. Assumptions: streams use the observed $FE/$FD control-token encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, indirect-pointer scratch, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

records.s: [offcut 4564] Self-modified immediate operand of `LDY #$00` at `$4563`. The Central Park music sequencer writes the selected sequence index here at `$4531`; the following indexed table reads install the sequence pointer in `$FE/$FF`.

records.c: Immediate Y operand in LDY #index at $4563. $4531 rewrites it from instrument byte 1 before selecting the pitch sequence. This is a self-modified operand, not an independent routine; execution continues at $4565.

Loads the selected four-entry pitch-sequence pointer, reads the current per-voice cursor $4072, handles $FD/$FE control and $FF redirection, updates frequency-high state $4081, clears $407E and advances the cursor. The $4592 branch advances the cursor then restores the note frequency through $45C3. Uses the instrument-selected index embedded in the preceding LDY operand.

Purpose: advance a voice's auxiliary effect sequence. Inputs: selected voice and its auxiliary pointer and cursor. Outputs: the next auxiliary value or control state is installed. Assumptions: the pointer addresses a valid phase-local auxiliary sequence. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, cursor state, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: load a note's target frequency into the selected voice state. Inputs: note-table index and voice-state index. Outputs: target-frequency low and high bytes are updated. Assumptions: both indices are valid for the phase-local frequency tables. Clobbers: A, indexed voice state, and flags. Hardware changes: none directly; this routine does not write SID registers.

Purpose: move current pitch toward its target under the current pitch-step rule. Inputs: current and target frequency plus signed step state. Outputs: current frequency is stepped and clamped, with a next target loaded when required. Assumptions: the paired frequency bytes and step state are internally consistent. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice arithmetic scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: update one voice's pitch envelope for the current music tick. Inputs: voice index, envelope cursor, current frequency, and envelope stream. Outputs: frequency, cursor, and envelope counters are advanced. Assumptions: the active envelope pointer addresses a valid stream. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: conditionally initialize one voice's modulation stream. Inputs: X selects the voice, Y selects its modulation definition, and the current per-voice guard controls initialization. Outputs: when the guard is zero, the modulation cursor and count are cleared and the definition's mode bit is installed; otherwise voice state is unchanged. Assumptions: X and Y index valid phase-local voice and definition records. Clobbers: A and flags, plus indexed voice state only on the initialization path; X and Y are preserved. Hardware changes: none directly.

Purpose: execute one modulation-stream step. Inputs: selected voice, modulation cursor and count, and current frequency. Outputs: cursor, count, and modulated frequency are updated. Assumptions: the stream follows the observed signed-update and control-token encoding. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and voice scratch. Hardware changes: none directly.

Indexed reads based at $4A41-$4A50 supply filter frequency/routing, volume-high bits, envelope control, stream pointer, bounds and signed increments. Slots are shared by these two consumers; source table membership does not imply that every slot is selected.

Eight-byte song descriptor: primary and secondary tick-divider reloads, followed by three little-endian voice playlist pointers. $40B1 multiplies song index by eight and copies these fields into music state. Captured descriptor zero points to $4AB9, $4B10 and $4B59. Only this intact descriptor is established in the retained Central Park image.
Secondary divider field and indexed high-byte alias within the song descriptor at $4AB1; not the beginning of a separate stream allocation.

Voice 0 playlist at $4AB9-$4B0F, selected by song descriptor zero. $4183 onward handles phrase ids, transpose, repeated-phrase and timing control; $FF redirects the playlist cursor using the following byte. All three boundaries are fixed by the descriptor and the following phrase directory.

19 low bytes of phrase pointers; $4221 selects one with Y and $4226 reads the corresponding high byte at $4B91. The directory includes interior entries into shared phrase data, so streams are not forced into disjoint records.
19 high bytes paired with $4B7E. The phrase pool begins at $4BA4 and ends at $4DE3, immediately before the scene header.

Scene header: first byte is 118, the number of scene pointers processed by the one-time relocation loop at $8A15. The following delta word at $4DE5/$4DE6 is $0800 in the fresh captured level. The area scene-selector bytes start at $4DE7; scene pointers begin at $4E27. The loaded pointers are already relocatable biased words; after initialization the entry at $8A0F is patched to RTS.

32 two-byte area slots at $4DE7-$4E26: scene selector then background/color flags. $8A54 doubles current area into X, $8A56 reads byte 1 and masks its low nibble for $D021, while $8A64 reads byte 0 and doubles the scene selector to index the scene directory. A $FF scene selects the renderer sentinel path. Populated Central Park slots are followed by $FF/0 pairs.

Background/color byte of area slot zero in the paired array $4DE7-$4E26. Read at $8A56 using X=2*area; low nibble becomes VIC-II background $D021 and renderer color $32. It is not an independent per-area scene array.
